title: Mice inheriting fear of acetophenone

tellings.quote: well when they were published in in nature there was that the title was inheriting the fear of fathers

plain: A biologist, Rupert Sheldrake, describes an experiment at a US university where mice were taught to fear acetophenone, a chemical with a sweet smell. He says the results were published in Nature, a leading science journal, under a title about inheriting the fear of fathers, meaning the offspring seemed to fear the smell too. If so, it would mean learned memories can pass from parent to child.
